transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband services. My name is Vicky. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Vicky. I have been paying forty-five pounds every month for S-Net's five hundred megabit full fiber broadband for the past four months, but whenever I run speed tests on my laptop, the download speed is strictly hard-capped at exactly ten megabits per second! I have spent four months paying premium prices for dial-up speeds while trying to stream video lectures and download MRI files for my university medical degree, and I am sick and tired of being ripped off!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open your broadband account ledger and physical provisioning docket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The optical terminal serial number on our hallway wall box is ALCL-B nine two zero one nine eight four.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please hold while I query the Openreach optical line profile database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Vicky, are you still there? The line went totally silent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies for the pause. The optical profile database indicates that your optical ONT is locked to an emergency provisioning profile of ten megabits symmetrical.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: An emergency ten megabit profile?! Why on earth is our optical box locked to an emergency ten megabit profile when we pay for five hundred megabits?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When your broadband contract was migrated from your previous student rental flat four months ago, the automated order completion script encountered an XML synchronization error between our legacy billing database and the wholesale radius server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So your automated computer system had an XML bug four months ago, and S-Net just left us capped at ten megabits while happily charging our bank forty-five pounds every month?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The wholesale provisioning platform does not flag bandwidth profile mismatches automatically unless a manual service audit is initiated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you immediately reprovision the line to five hundred megabits right now so I can download my coursework?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me examine the central RADIUS subscriber management portal on our network core.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have a two-gigabyte medical imaging lecture file that has been failing to download all morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, the optical terminal serial number on your wall box is ALCL-B nine two zero one nine eight four?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, ALCL-B nine two zero one nine eight four is printed directly on the barcode label beneath the power switch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you connect your laptop to the optical terminal, are you plugging directly into LAN port 1 with an Ethernet cable or connecting over Wi-Fi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I tested with a brand-new Cat6 Ethernet cable plugged directly into LAN port 1, and the speed test tops out at exactly nine point eight megabits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the Ethernet port LED on the optical terminal illuminate green or amber when the laptop is connected?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The LED is amber, showing that the physical port is negotiating at ten megabits rather than gigabit ethernet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An amber port link confirms that the optical terminal's internal policer chip is rate-limiting the hardware interface to ten megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Which proves that your wholesale system is actively throttling our hardware port!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What optical light power level reading is registered on the internal photodiode receiver?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The telemetry status page displays minus eighteen point four dBm, which is well within normal limits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Minus eighteen point four dBm confirms that optical signal attenuation across the physical fiber path is completely nominal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the physical fiber cable on the street is completely perfect and has zero optical loss!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What specific download file transfers are failing or timing out during your medical coursework?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am downloading 3D volumetric DICOM MRI patient scan datasets from the university hospital server, where each dataset contains twelve hundred high-resolution axial slices totaling one point eight gigabytes, and the hospital web proxy aborts the connection after thirty minutes because the ten-megabit cap takes over forty minutes to complete!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When single-stream TCP file transfers exceed web proxy timeout thresholds, the host server automatically resets the connection socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly! Which is why being capped at ten megabits when I pay for five hundred megabits is ruining my university studies!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please hold while I check whether the wholesale provisioning queue can accept a manual profile push.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Vicky, hello? Did the call drop out again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, thank you for waiting. The central RADIUS provisioning server is currently locked in an automated database reconciliation freeze for end-of-month billing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So can you push the five hundred megabit profile or not?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the database reconciliation freeze is active, any manual speed profile update must wait until your next monthly billing cycle resets on the twelfth of next month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait until the twelfth of next month?! That is three whole weeks away! You expect me to study for final university exams on a throttled ten megabit connection for three more weeks after already suffering four months of this?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Company provisioning procedures strictly forbid manual database overrides while central reconciliation batch jobs are executing across subscriber ledgers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not escalate this to a network operations supervisor or tier-three engineering desk who has root database clearance?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tier-three engineering does not accept provisioning ticket escalations for residential accounts during automated billing freezes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is an absolute disgrace! S-Net has stolen forty-five pounds a month from me, throttled my broadband to dial-up speeds, and now refuses to press a button to fix it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ten megabit profile provides basic connectivity for standard web text browsing and light messaging.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am studying digital radiology and downloading 3D MRI scans, not reading text messages! Can S-Net at least refund the four months of overcharged subscription fees?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Billing refund requests can only be evaluated after the technical speed fault is officially closed and verified by wholesale reconciliation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you won't fix the speed today, you won't escalate to an engineer, and you won't even refund the overcharges!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged the provisioning mismatch ticket under reference PRV-66102-S.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: PRV-66102-S. I am lodging an immediate dispute with the communications ombudsman and the credit card company.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ticket notes will be processed by wholesale provisioning once the monthly billing reconciliation window terminates.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When the profile finally resets on the twelfth, how will I know the gigabit speed is active?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The amber Ethernet LED on the optical terminal will switch to solid green, confirming that the physical port is negotiating at full gigabit speeds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will inspect that Ethernet port LED on the twelfth to make sure it switches from amber to green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A solid green link indicator confirms full five hundred megabit hardware throughput.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our mobile phone network with EE in this apartment gets four bars of 5G, so fortunately I can tether my phone in emergencies even though mobile data is expensive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Third-party cellular networks operate independently of fixed-line fiber optical distribution networks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, thank goodness they do, otherwise I would have failed my university term completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: High-capacity 5G cellular masts provide robust emergency fallback data during fixed-line provisioning delays.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait Vicky, if the profile resets on the twelfth, will the router automatically reboot itself or do I need to power cycle...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a good afternoon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait Vicky, do I need to power cycle... hello?
